title: Conditional types
explain: A conditional type picks one type or another with the shape `T extends U ? X : Y`. With `infer` it can also capture part of a type, such as a function's return type. These are the building blocks behind built-in helpers like `ReturnType` and `Awaited`.
exercise: Write `Unwrap<T>` that turns `Promise<string>` into `string` and leaves other types alone.
tip: A conditional type spreads over unions, so `IsString<string | number>` gives `"yes" | "no"`. Wrap `T` in a tuple like `[T]` to stop that.
